subject: Is it possible to compare groups with different landmarks?

messages.author: 248af1cd72d9f2d5
messages.subject: Is it possible to compare groups with different landmarks?
parts:
I have a developmental series where cartilage is formed at different times. I would like to place landmarks on the cartilage at two different developmental stages and was wondering what the best way of doing this was when some structures don't exist in one developmental stage compared to the other?

I imagine that placing as many similar landmarks as possible between each dev.stage, then removing those extra landmarks when it comes down to analysing dev.stage differences would be an option....is there another way?

Thanks! :-)
Sam

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Is it possible to compare groups with different landmarks?
parts:
Sam,

 

For GM analyses one does require a common set of landmarks, as these are the anatomical ‘bits’ that derive correspondence across specimens. This is directly akin to what one does with other biological comprisons: compare length vs. length across groups, or genetic variation in CytB vs. CytB across groups. Makes little sense to try to compare groups using different subsets of variables.


With GM, when there are some non-corresponding landmarks, two options are possible. First, one may remove the landmarks present in group A but not in group B, so the remaining set of landmarks is common to both. Alternatively, one may attempt to estimate the positions of missing landmarks using imputation methods. Two such methods have been examined in the context of GM and both are in geomorph. Note that before using these I would strongly recommend reading the primary literature on the topic. One may find useful references in the help file for the function ‘estimate.missing.’

 

Dean
